terminologyReview: Guideline clarification: the revised distinction in references/common.md and references/ga.md is correct. The evidence agrees on three points. intl-workerd.json shows Intl.ListFormat and Intl.RelativeTimeFormat unsupported (English output) for eo, be and ga, while Intl.PluralRules returns native categories for all 18 locales. InstructionTemplates (packages/shared/src/instruction-template.ts) builds Intl.PluralRules for the content language and throws when a catalog omits a native count variant or a message. BotText.andList and transcriptLabelList join items only through the catalog's formatting.* patterns. So Bickr's own formatters never 'silently return English'; the English fallback is only a property of the platform Intl list and relative-time formatters, which Bickr does not use for these strings. One leftover: references/eo.md line 7 still says 'The runtime formatters silently return English, although plural rules work.' It should use the same wording as common.md and ga.md (be.md already does). This is a guideline edit only and changes no frozen English unit.

Ukrainian terminology follows the lead decisions. "підписуватися" is used for follow (no "стежити" left). Relative time uses native fragments with per-category case forms. "давніше" is used for older notifications. No first-person past predicate or pronoun marks the participant's gender. "ref" stays the defined prose term, consistent with system.main. All changed count units were checked for 1, 2, 5, 21, 101 and a fractional value.

grok.terminologyReview: The revised Workers boundary is correct. Intl.ListFormat and Intl.RelativeTimeFormat fall back to English for Esperanto, Belarusian, and Irish, while Intl.PluralRules supports native categories. Bickr catalog formatters use explicit translated patterns and reject a missing entry, so the older phrase that runtime formatters silently return English does not describe Bickr. Ukrainian is outside that fallback set. These time phrases are explicit catalog text. Ukrainian one is 1, 21, and 101. few is 2, 3, and 4. many includes 0 and the genitive plural. other is the fractional genitive singular. підписуватися is the follow action. учасник is the role noun, and agreement with it does not assign a person’s gender. давніше is the older-notification term, spelled with і. A detached member heading stays nominative, with singular Учасник only in one. ref remains the defined prose term. The comparison note about formal gender-neutral narration is not an open question: мною and impersonal forms keep the actor and the completed action without a gendered first-person past.
